seoTitle: How to Add Music to a Canva Website Easily
metaDescription: Embed background music on your live Canva website using the Audio Player app to add an interactive track list, playlist, or single-song widget.
intro: Canva websites don't autoplay background audio, but that's not actually a limitation once you know where the Audio Player app lives — it gives visitors a real, interactive player instead of a track that starts without their consent. This guide follows the actual app: installing it from Canva's Apps library, picking a template that matches what you want to embed, and configuring the finished widget with your own tracks.

steps.heading: Open the Audio Player app from your website workspace
steps.body: From your active website project, open the Apps panel in the sidebar and find Audio Player — a free app dedicated specifically to embedding playable tracks. On first opening it, you'll land on its overview screen showing your widget usage (0 of 1 on the free tier) and view count, with a prompt reading "Your first widget is almost here!" and a Create Widget button front and center.

image.caption: The Audio Player app's overview screen inside Canva, showing widget and view limits on the free plan and a "Create Widget" button to get started.

steps.heading: Choose a template that matches your content
steps.body: Clicking Create Widget opens a template picker with several starting points: Music Playlist, Inline Audio Player, Single Track, New Album, Meditation & Ambience, and Audiobook. Each template previews live on the right — the Audiobook option, for example, shows a full cover-art player with chapter tracks and running times listed underneath, which is exactly the kind of layout worth picking if you're embedding a multi-track playlist rather than one standalone song.

image.caption: The Audio Player template picker, with Music Playlist, Inline Audio Player, Single Track, and Audiobook options, and a live preview of the selected template on the right.

steps.heading: Add your tracks to the widget
steps.body: Once you continue with a template, the editor splits into a Tracks panel on the left — where you can add, reorder, or remove individual songs or chapters — and a live preview on the right showing exactly how the player will look and behave once published. Each track needs its own audio source; there's no bulk-upload shortcut, so building out a full playlist means adding entries one at a time.

image.caption: The configured Audio Player widget, with a full track list on the left and a live cover-art preview of the player on the right.

steps.heading: Adjust the layout and style
steps.body: The same editor panel includes Layout, Style, and Settings tabs alongside Tracks, letting you switch how the player displays, adjust its color scheme to match your site, and control playback behavior like autoplay-on-click or loop settings. These are worth reviewing before you place the widget, since changing the layout after positioning it on the page can shift its dimensions and require you to resize it again.

steps.heading: Position the widget inside your page grid
steps.body: Drag the finished widget onto your website page and resize it to fit neatly inside your existing grid sections rather than letting it float awkwardly between other elements. Canva websites are built on the same grid-based layout as the rest of the design tool, so the player widget behaves like any other element you'd resize and align — snap it to nearby edges for a cleaner result.

steps.heading: Publish and test playback on the live page
steps.body: Publish your site and open the live URL to confirm the player actually loads and plays as expected — a widget that looks right in the editor can still behave differently once it's rendered on the published page, especially across mobile versus desktop. Click through the play, skip, and track-list controls yourself before sharing the link, since a broken player on a musician portfolio or podcast landing page undercuts the whole point of adding it.

faq.question: Will the music autoplay when visitors land on my site?
faq.answer: No — Canva websites don't support autoplaying background tracks, so visitors need to click play on the embedded Audio Player widget themselves.

faq.question: Can I upload my own audio file instead of using Spotify?
faq.answer: The Audio Player app is built around adding tracks directly inside its Tracks panel rather than pasting an external streaming link, so you add and manage each track from within the widget editor.

faq.question: Will the player look the same on mobile?
faq.answer: The widget resizes with your layout grid, but it's worth previewing your published site on mobile specifically to confirm the player still looks and functions correctly at a smaller size.

faq.question: Do I need a Canva Pro plan to embed audio?
faq.answer: The Audio Player app has a free tier with a limited widget and view count, so you can try it without upgrading, though heavier use may require a paid plan.

faq.question: What templates does the Audio Player app offer?
faq.answer: It includes Music Playlist, Inline Audio Player, Single Track, New Album, Meditation & Ambience, and Audiobook templates, each with a different layout suited to different kinds of content.
